doc.title: BWI ATCT SOP
doc.summary: Standard operating procedures for Baltimore (BWI) ATCT positions: positions/frequencies, East/West runway configurations, clearance delivery (climb via SIDs, altitude restrictions, departure gates, frequencies), ground taxi splits, local control airspace, departure headings, releases and go-around procedures.

items.title: Purpose, audience, cancellation, changes
items.text: Order describes airspace, procedures and control policy for all controllers working a BWI ATCT position on VATSIM; applies to all vZDC controllers and visiting controllers training with vZDC. Cancels BWI ATCT SOP Version G dated 5 July 2024. Version H adds vTDLS guidance, IDS Departure Release Requests during TMIs, climb via for all BWI SIDs, and tower assumed radar identification (bulletins vZDC-BWI-B-2050707, vZDC-B-20250923A, vZDC-BWI-B-20251207). Changes are shaded grey.

items.title: Word and term meanings
items.text: Arrivals/Departures refer specifically to aircraft on an IFR flight plan. VFR Arrival/VFR Departure refer to aircraft arriving/departing under VFR. Delegated Airspace is airspace assigned to a specific sector or position within a facility.

items.title: Abbreviations
items.text: AOA = at or above; AOB = at or below; CHP = Chesapeake Area of Potomac TRACON; PCT = Potomac TRACON (entire facility); FRZ = Flight Restriction Zone; SFRA = Special Flight Rules Area; TDLS = Tower Data-link System; STARS = terminal radar software of vNAS and CRC; ZDC = Washington ARTCC; ATAP = Automated Terminal Proximity Alert.

items.title: Clearance Delivery (CD) 118.05
items.text: Clearance Delivery, position ID CD, STARS handoff Not assigned, frequency 118.05. CD combines to GC1.

items.title: Ground West (GC1) 121.9
items.text: Ground West, position ID GC1, STARS handoff 11, frequency 121.9. Primary frequency. GC1 combines to LC1.

items.title: Ground East (GC2) 120.2
items.text: Ground East, position ID GC2, STARS handoff Not assigned, frequency 120.2. GC2 combines to GC1.

items.title: Local West (LC1) 119.4
items.text: Local West, position ID LC1, STARS handoff 11, frequency 119.4. Primary frequency. Performs CIC function when CIC not staffed.

items.title: Local East (LC2) 123.75
items.text: Local East, position ID LC2, STARS handoff Not assigned, frequency 123.75. LC2 combines to LC1.

items.title: Controller in Charge (CIC)
items.text: Controller in Charge, position ID CIC, STARS handoff Not assigned, frequency Not assigned. CIC function is performed by LC1 when not staffed.

items.title: Non-standard runway configurations
items.text: Preferred configurations are in 2-2-2 and 2-2-3. Local control may use non-standard runway configurations as weather/traffic permit, so long as the configuration does not negatively affect traffic flow, is necessary due to weather and traffic conditions, and PCT is aware of it.

items.title: East Ops: 15R jet dep, 10 jet arr, 15L GA
items.text: East Operations: Runway 15R is the primary departure runway for all turbojet aircraft. Runway 15L is the preferred arrival and departure runway for general aviation aircraft. Runway 10 is the primary arrival runway for turbojet aircraft.

items.title: West Ops: 28 jet dep, 33L jet arr, 33R GA
items.text: West Operations: Runway 28 is the primary departure runway for all turbojet aircraft. Runway 33R is the preferred arrival and departure runway for general aviation aircraft. Runway 33L is the primary arrival runway for turbojet aircraft. West Operations is the calm wind configuration; use it when wind is less than 5 knots.

items.title: Routine runway configuration change
items.text: CIC determines the need for active runway changes; in a routine change departures may depart the runway originally assigned. Provide PCT the last departure's ID, estimated departure time and runway; after it departs no other aircraft departs BWI without a release from PCT. Ensure departures off the new runway have the right departure procedure/instructions and departure frequency; PCT informs CIC when sector reconfiguration is complete; update the ATIS.

items.title: ASDE-X: Mode C and safety logic alerts
items.text: GC and LC ensure all aircraft in a movement area have transponders on with Mode C. Configure ASDE-X safety logic for EAST or WEST operations. If an airborne arrival (prior to the landing threshold) activates a warning alert, issue go-around instructions; if two arrivals, or an arrival and a departure, activate an alert, issue go-around or take action to ensure intersecting runway separation. Other alerts: use good judgment. Review FAAO 7110.65 Ch 3 Sec 6.

items.title: DC SFRA at BWI
items.text: DC SFRA procedures are simulated with a modified procedure. VFR departures are expected to file a DC SFRA flight plan. The FRZ does not impose higher requirements, so normal VFR operations including pattern work are allowed if workload permits. Ref: VATSIM DC SFRA Procedures / Pilot Guide; vZDC-PCT-P-01G Ch 2 Sec 8.
items.restr: VFR dep file SFRA flight plan

items.title: CD duties; TMI-constrained departures via IDS
items.text: CD formulates and issues IFR and VFR clearances to BWI departures and reviews/amends routes and altitudes per LOAs. For aircraft departing to a constrained airport (TMI such as EDCT or Call for Release), CD coordinates with the pilot for expected pushback/taxi time, submits a departure release request through IDS, advises the pilot of the anticipated wheels up time, and ensures GC and LC are aware (considered coordinated when the correct release time shows in the IDS released aircraft list).

items.title: IFR clearance: SID climb via, else 4,000
items.text: All IFR departures should be assigned a departure and transition consistent with their direction of flight. Aircraft unable to fly a SID are assigned radar vectors to their initial fix. Climb via SID for all aircraft on a SID; all other aircraft get an initial altitude of 4,000 feet and expect filed cruise altitude ten minutes after departure.
items.restr: Climb via SID; non-SID 4,000, exp filed 10 min

items.title: vTDLS PDC for eligible IFR aircraft
items.text: BWI is equipped with vTDLS to issue Pre-Departure Clearances (PDCs) to IFR aircraft. TDLS shall be used for all eligible aircraft unless a voice clearance is more operationally advantageous. Ref: vZDC-A-01F para 4-1-4.

items.title: VFR flight following plan requirements
items.text: VFR aircraft requesting flight following shall have destination airport, aircraft type and requested VFR altitude in their VFR flight plan prior to departure. Use of the STARS VFR flight plan entry function is encouraged.

items.title: VFR Class B clearance: maintain VFR AOB
items.text: VFR aircraft remaining in the pattern are assigned a VFR code and need no altitude restriction. All VFR departures receive a Class B clearance to maintain VFR at or below 3,500 for turboprop and turbojet aircraft, and 2,000 for propeller and helicopter aircraft.

items.title: East/Southeast departures: GRACO 124.55
items.text: Assign departure frequency per SID, departure gate or direction of flight: East/Southeast departures get GRACO/1G (124.55).

items.title: SW/West/North departures: WOOLY 128.7
items.text: Assign departure frequency per SID, departure gate or direction of flight: Southwest/West/North departures get WOOLY/1W (128.7).

items.title: Expected final cruise altitude by destination
items.text: IFR aircraft destined to airports in TBL 3-2-1 are assigned an expected final cruise altitude per the table. Pilots may request higher with PCT or ZDC once airborne; it may be approved as an operational request.

items.title: BWI to DCA, IAD, HEF: final altitude
items.text: BWI IFR departures destined to DCA, IAD, HEF: expected final cruise altitude 4,000 for turbojets; turboprop/propeller 4,000. Pilots may request higher from PCT/ZDC once airborne.

items.title: BWI to EWR, TEB, LGA: final altitude
items.text: BWI IFR departures destined to EWR, TEB, LGA: expected final cruise altitude FL210 for turbojets; turboprop/propeller N/A. Pilots may request higher from PCT/ZDC once airborne.

items.title: BWI to JFK: final altitude
items.text: BWI IFR departures destined to JFK: expected final cruise altitude 17,000 for turbojets; turboprop/propeller N/A. Pilots may request higher from PCT/ZDC once airborne.

items.title: BWI to MTN: final altitude
items.text: BWI IFR departures destined to MTN: expected final cruise altitude 3,000 for turbojets; turboprop/propeller 3,000. Pilots may request higher from PCT/ZDC once airborne.

items.title: BWI to ORF: final altitude
items.text: BWI IFR departures destined to ORF: expected final cruise altitude 14,000 for turbojets; turboprop/propeller N/A. Pilots may request higher from PCT/ZDC once airborne.

items.title: BWI to PHL: final altitude
items.text: BWI IFR departures destined to PHL: expected final cruise altitude 11,000 for turbojets; turboprop/propeller 7,000. Pilots may request higher from PCT/ZDC once airborne.

items.title: BWI to RIC: final altitude
items.text: BWI IFR departures destined to RIC: expected final cruise altitude 14,000 for turbojets; turboprop/propeller 10,000. Pilots may request higher from PCT/ZDC once airborne.

items.title: IFR departures exit PCT via departure gates
items.text: PCT uses departure exit gates for IFR departures to destinations outside PCT airspace. Every IFR aircraft leaving BWI must leave PCT airspace bound for one of these gates unless coordinated otherwise.

items.title: High altitude gates: filed above 10,000
items.text: High altitude departure gates should be used for aircraft filed above 10,000 feet. Prop and turboprop aircraft may be routed via a low altitude gate regardless of altitude. Ref: vZDC-PCT-P-01G para 6-4-11.

items.title: High gate BUFFR (NW)
items.text: BWI high altitude departure gate BUFFR, routing/direction NW. For aircraft filed above 10,000 feet.

items.title: High gate CLTCH (SW)
items.text: BWI high altitude departure gate CLTCH, routing/direction SW. For aircraft filed above 10,000 feet.

items.title: High gate DAILY/COLIN (S/SE)
items.text: BWI high altitude departure gate DAILY/COLIN, routing/direction S/SE. For aircraft filed above 10,000 feet.

items.title: High gate JERES (N/NW)
items.text: BWI high altitude departure gate JERES, routing/direction N/NW. For aircraft filed above 10,000 feet.

items.title: High gate JDUBB (SW)
items.text: BWI high altitude departure gate JDUBB, routing/direction SW. For aircraft filed above 10,000 feet.

items.title: High gate OTTTO (W)
items.text: BWI high altitude departure gate OTTTO, routing/direction W. For aircraft filed above 10,000 feet.

items.title: High gate PALEO (NE)
items.text: BWI high altitude departure gate PALEO, routing/direction NE. For aircraft filed above 10,000 feet.

items.title: High gate RAMAY (W)
items.text: BWI high altitude departure gate RAMAY, routing/direction W. For aircraft filed above 10,000 feet.

items.title: High gate SCRAM (SW)
items.text: BWI high altitude departure gate SCRAM, routing/direction SW. For aircraft filed above 10,000 feet.

items.title: High gate SWANN (NE)
items.text: BWI high altitude departure gate SWANN, routing/direction NE. For aircraft filed above 10,000 feet.

items.title: High gate WOOLY (NE)
items.text: BWI high altitude departure gate WOOLY, routing/direction NE. For aircraft filed above 10,000 feet.

items.title: Low altitude gates: filed AOB 10,000
items.text: Low altitude departure gates should be used for aircraft filed at or below 10,000 feet. Low altitude aircraft may receive vectors to join any low altitude airway.

items.title: Low gate CSN (W/SW)
items.text: BWI low altitude departure gate CSN, routing/direction W/SW. For aircraft filed at or below 10,000 feet (props/turboprops may use regardless of altitude).

items.title: Low gate EMI (N/NE)
items.text: BWI low altitude departure gate EMI, routing/direction N/NE. For aircraft filed at or below 10,000 feet (props/turboprops may use regardless of altitude).

items.title: Low gate GVE (S/SW)
items.text: BWI low altitude departure gate GVE, routing/direction S/SW. For aircraft filed at or below 10,000 feet (props/turboprops may use regardless of altitude).

items.title: Low gate MRB (N/NW)
items.text: BWI low altitude departure gate MRB, routing/direction N/NW. For aircraft filed at or below 10,000 feet (props/turboprops may use regardless of altitude).

items.title: Low gate PXT (SE)
items.text: BWI low altitude departure gate PXT, routing/direction SE. For aircraft filed at or below 10,000 feet (props/turboprops may use regardless of altitude).

items.title: Ground control duties
items.text: Ground Control sequences aircraft having the same first fix or direction of departure with other aircraft, and keeps runway exits clear for landing aircraft.

items.title: No blanket runway crossings
items.text: Blanket crossings are not approved at BWI. Ground control must verbally coordinate with local control for any aircraft requiring a runway crossing.

items.title: East Ops turbojets depart Runway 15R
items.text: In East operation, assign turbojets departing BWI Runway 15R. Assigning a non-standard runway requires coordination with local control (verbal or nonverbal).

items.title: East Ops props depart Runway 15L
items.text: In East operation, assign props departing BWI Runway 15L. Assigning a non-standard runway requires coordination with local control (verbal or nonverbal).

items.title: West Ops turbojets depart Runway 28
items.text: In West operation, assign turbojets departing BWI Runway 28. Assigning a non-standard runway requires coordination with local control (verbal or nonverbal).

items.title: West Ops props depart Runway 33R
items.text: In West operation, assign props departing BWI Runway 33R. Assigning a non-standard runway requires coordination with local control (verbal or nonverbal).

items.title: Ground East area: east of Pier C
items.text: Ground East (GC2) is responsible for movement areas east of Pier C as depicted in Appendix A.

items.title: Ground East, West Ops: Bravo/Charlie to Rwy 28
items.text: When in West operation, Ground East shall use taxiways Bravo and Charlie for runway 28 departures.

items.title: Ground East, East Ops: 15R dep handoff to GC West
items.text: When in East operation, Ground East instructs runway 15R departures to hold short of taxiway Uniform on taxiway Tango, or hold short of taxiway Tango on taxiway Alpha; once holding short, transfer to Ground West.
items.restr: HS U on T / HS T on A, then GC1

items.title: Ground West area: west of Pier C
items.text: Ground West (GC1) is responsible for movement areas west of Pier C as depicted in Appendix A.

items.title: Ground West, West Ops: Uniform to 28; 33R to GC East
items.text: When in West operation, Ground West uses taxiway Uniform for runway 28 departures. For aircraft requesting runway 33R, instruct them to hold short of taxiway Uniform on taxiway Tango; once holding short, transfer to Ground East.
items.restr: 28 via U; 33R: HS U on T, then GC2

items.title: Ground West, East Ops: 15R taxi; 15L to GC East
items.text: When in East operation, Ground West receives runway 15R aircraft from Ground East on taxiways Tango and Alpha and continues taxiing them to 15R. For aircraft requesting runway 15L, instruct them to hold short of taxiway Uniform on taxiway Papa; once holding short, transfer to Ground East.
items.restr: 15L: HS U on P, then GC2

items.title: Pushbacks onto A and T; tail direction
items.text: Ground approves pushbacks onto taxiways A and T, specifying tail direction (e.g. PUSHBACK ON ALPHA APPROVED, TAIL WEST). During high volume such as events, GC may approve pushbacks for aircraft that would push into a non-movement area; if TMIs are in effect, instruct affected aircraft to advise ready for pushback. Ground West approves pushbacks into the non-movement area between pier B and C.

items.title: Local Control airspace around BAL
items.text: Local Control assumes responsibility for airspace within 5 NM of BAL at and below 3,000 feet, and between 5 NM and 7 NM of BAL below 1,500 feet.

items.title: Local East: 15L/33R and App B/C airspace
items.text: Local East (LC2) is responsible for the airspace depicted in Appendix B and C and runway 15L/33R. Appendices show the LC split line through the airport with the outer ring AOB 1499 and inner ring AOB 3000, Local East to the north/east side.

items.title: Local West: 15R/33L, 10/28 and App B/C airspace
items.text: Local West (LC1) is responsible for the airspace depicted in Appendix B and C and runways 15R/33L and 10/28. Appendices show Local West on the south/west side of the split, AOB 3000 inner area and AOB 1499 outer ring.

items.title: Headings only for non-SID departures
items.text: Assign an initial heading for departures not cleared via a SID. Aircraft cleared via a SID shall not be issued a departure heading unless necessary for traffic and coordinated with PCT prior to takeoff clearance.
items.restr: SID: no heading unless coord PCT

items.title: East Ops turbojets departure headings
items.text: East Operation departure headings for turbojets not on a SID: WOOLY departure sector 330; GRACO departure sector 120 – 150.

items.title: East Ops props departure headings
items.text: East Operation departure headings for props not on a SID: WOOLY departure sector 040 – 120; GRACO departure sector 100 – 120.

items.title: West Ops turbojets departure headings
items.text: West Operation departure headings for turbojets not on a SID: WOOLY departure sector 270 – 290; GRACO departure sector 150.

items.title: West Ops props departure headings
items.text: West Operation departure headings for props not on a SID: WOOLY departure sector 310 – 330; GRACO departure sector 360 – 030.

items.title: LUAW authorized
items.text: LUAW is authorized at BWI. Use it when the aircraft is expected to depart after conflicting traffic is clear of the runway/intersection, using good operating practices and memory aids. Landing clearances need not be withheld for traffic holding in position.

items.title: Automatic departures and suspension
items.text: Automatic departures are authorized. Aircraft under a TMI (EDCT or call for release) must depart within their release validity period. Automatic departures are suspended until PCT restores them when: the previous arrival conducts an unplanned go around and automatic releases are not granted on initial go around coordination from PCT; PCT cancels automatic releases; or an aircraft departs a non-standard (non ATIS advertised) runway.

items.title: Release request content; valid 5 minutes
items.text: While automatic departures are suspended, Local Control calls PCT for release stating callsign, departure runway, and SID and transition, initial fix, or heading to be assigned. Releases are valid for 5 minutes unless otherwise coordinated at time of release.

items.title: Tower assumed radar ID before departure switch
items.text: Before switching a departure to PCT, local must observe it acquire on the STARS TDW within one mile of the departure end of runway; once correctly acquired it may be switched. If acquisition does not occur, notify the PCT departure controller before the frequency change with callsign and SID or assigned heading. The primary departure sector uses autotrack for all BWI departures.

items.title: Missed approach/go around coordination
items.text: Local Control immediately coordinates with PCT when an IFR aircraft goes around and, unless otherwise coordinated, issues TBL 5-3-2 instructions. Automatic releases are suspended after a missed approach/go around until released by PCT. Tower may re-sequence props if it ensures separation from all pertinent traffic and does not affect the sequence of other IFR arrivals sequenced by PCT.

items.title: Go around rwy 10/33L: 2,000, hdg 200
items.text: Missed approach/go around instructions for runway 10/33L: altitude 2,000, heading 200, unless otherwise coordinated with PCT.

items.title: Go around rwy 15L/33R: 2,000, hdg 060
items.text: Missed approach/go around instructions for runway 15L/33R: altitude 2,000, heading 060, unless otherwise coordinated with PCT.

items.title: Go around rwy Other: 2,000, rwy hdg
items.text: Missed approach/go around for all other runways: altitude 2,000, fly runway heading, unless otherwise coordinated with PCT.

items.title: Transfer to ground once clear of runway
items.text: Once aircraft are clear of the runway they shall be transferred to ground control unless otherwise coordinated.
